lead_tasks.title: Obtain MCST renovation approval
lead_tasks.description: Submit a renovation application to your condominium's Management Corporation Strata Title (MCST) for approval before starting any works.

lead_tasks.title: Pay MCST renovation security deposit
lead_tasks.description: Pay the required security deposit to the condo management before commencing renovation. Amount varies by condo.

lead_tasks.title: Engage Licensed Electrical Worker (LEW)
lead_tasks.description: All electrical work must be carried out or supervised by an EMA-licensed LEW. This includes installation, repair, or modification of wiring and power points.

lead_tasks.title: Engage PUB Licensed Plumber
lead_tasks.description: All regulated water service and sanitary plumbing works must be carried out by a PUB Licensed Plumber (LP). It is an offence to engage an unlicensed plumber.

lead_tasks.title: Engage Licensed Gas Service Worker (LGSW) for gas works
lead_tasks.description: All gas pipe installation and modification works must be carried out by City Energy or an EMA-registered Licensed Gas Service Worker.

lead_tasks.title: Verify contractor meets MCST requirements
lead_tasks.description: Most MCSTs only approve renovation contractors who are BCA-licensed or registered under bizSAFE. Verify before submitting your MCST application.

lead_tasks.title: Engage PE/architect for structural modifications
lead_tasks.description: Structural modifications in condos require professional endorsement from a Professional Engineer or Registered Architect.

lead_tasks.title: Serve neighbour notification per MCST rules
lead_tasks.description: Check your MCST by-laws for neighbour notification or consent requirements and comply before starting works.

lead_tasks.title: No structural modifications without MCST + PE approval
lead_tasks.description: Alteration to structural elements (pillars, walls, beams, columns) in condos is prohibited without prior MCST approval and PE endorsement.

lead_tasks.title: Check concealed gas pipe locations before hacking
lead_tasks.description: Obtain a layout plan from condo management to identify concealed gas pipe locations before any drilling or hacking of walls.

lead_tasks.title: Book a second meeting with Nur
Call Cheryl back about her budget

quotes.title: Whole-home renovation
quotes.terms_html:
TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR RENOVATION WORKS

1. Agreement

These Terms and Conditions form part of the Renovation Contract entered into between the Homeowner/Client, Olivia Martinez, and the Contractor/Company, Demo Studio Pte Ltd, for the renovation works described in this quotation.

2. Scope of Works

The works are limited to the items listed in this quotation. Additional works, changes of material or changes to the approved drawings are variations and will be quoted and agreed in writing before they are carried out.

3. Validity and Pricing

This quotation is valid for 30 days from its date of issue. Prices are in Singapore dollars and include GST where stated. Quantities marked as estimates are re-measured on site before the relevant works begin.

4. Payment

Payment follows the schedule set out in this quotation. Works commence only after the deposit has been received. An invoice unpaid for more than 7 days may lead to the works being suspended until the outstanding amount is settled.

5. Timeline

The completion timeline is indicative and depends on material lead times, site access and the timely confirmation of drawings and selections. Demo Studio Pte Ltd will inform the Client of any change to the timeline as early as possible.

6. Permits and Compliance

Where a permit is required, Demo Studio Pte Ltd will apply for it on the Client’s behalf. All works comply with the guidelines of the relevant authorities and the building management, and any fee they impose is borne by the Client.

7. Materials and Warranty

Materials are as specified in this quotation or of equivalent quality where the specified item is unavailable. Workmanship for carpentry, wet works and electrical works is warranted for 12 months from handover, excluding wear and tear, misuse and alterations by other parties.

8. Cancellation

Should the Client cancel after the works have commenced, the Client pays for all works completed and materials ordered up to the date of cancellation.

For any query on these terms, contact Demo Studio Pte Ltd at 6222 0188. Prepared by Dane.
quotes.notes_html: Prices are inclusive of GST at 9%. Works are scheduled to start on about 15 Sep ’26 and run for about 10 weeks; the dates move with material lead times and the confirmation of selections.

TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR RENOVATION WORKS

1. Agreement

These Terms and Conditions form part of the Renovation Contract entered into between the Homeowner/Client, Harpreet Kaur, and the Contractor/Company, Demo Studio Pte Ltd, for the renovation works described in this quotation.

2. Scope of Works

The works are limited to the items listed in this quotation. Additional works, changes of material or changes to the approved drawings are variations and will be quoted and agreed in writing before they are carried out.

3. Validity and Pricing

This quotation is valid for 30 days from its date of issue. Prices are in Singapore dollars and include GST where stated. Quantities marked as estimates are re-measured on site before the relevant works begin.

4. Payment

Payment follows the schedule set out in this quotation. Works commence only after the deposit has been received. An invoice unpaid for more than 7 days may lead to the works being suspended until the outstanding amount is settled.

5. Timeline

The completion timeline is indicative and depends on material lead times, site access and the timely confirmation of drawings and selections. Demo Studio Pte Ltd will inform the Client of any change to the timeline as early as possible.

6. Permits and Compliance

Where a permit is required, Demo Studio Pte Ltd will apply for it on the Client’s behalf. All works comply with the guidelines of the relevant authorities and the building management, and any fee they impose is borne by the Client.

7. Materials and Warranty

Materials are as specified in this quotation or of equivalent quality where the specified item is unavailable. Workmanship for carpentry, wet works and electrical works is warranted for 12 months from handover, excluding wear and tear, misuse and alterations by other parties.

8. Cancellation

Should the Client cancel after the works have commenced, the Client pays for all works completed and materials ordered up to the date of cancellation.

For any query on these terms, contact Demo Studio Pte Ltd at 6222 0188. Prepared by Sarah.
quotes.notes_html: Prices are inclusive of GST at 9%. Works are scheduled to start on about 31 Aug ’26 and run for about 12 weeks; the dates move with material lead times and the confirmation of selections.

quote_text_templates.title: Terms and Conditions for Renovation Works
quote_text_templates.body:
TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR RENOVATION WORKS

1. Agreement

These Terms and Conditions form part of the Renovation Contract entered into between the Homeowner/Client, [Client Full Name], and the Contractor/Company, [Studio Name], for the renovation works described in this quotation.

2. Scope of Works

The works are limited to the items listed in this quotation. Additional works, changes of material or changes to the approved drawings are variations and will be quoted and agreed in writing before they are carried out.

3. Validity and Pricing

This quotation is valid for 30 days from its date of issue. Prices are in Singapore dollars and include GST where stated. Quantities marked as estimates are re-measured on site before the relevant works begin.

4. Payment

Payment follows the schedule set out in this quotation. Works commence only after the deposit has been received. An invoice unpaid for more than 7 days may lead to the works being suspended until the outstanding amount is settled.

5. Timeline

The completion timeline is indicative and depends on material lead times, site access and the timely confirmation of drawings and selections. [Studio Name] will inform the Client of any change to the timeline as early as possible.

6. Permits and Compliance

Where a permit is required, [Studio Name] will apply for it on the Client’s behalf. All works comply with the guidelines of the relevant authorities and the building management, and any fee they impose is borne by the Client.

7. Materials and Warranty

Materials are as specified in this quotation or of equivalent quality where the specified item is unavailable. Workmanship for carpentry, wet works and electrical works is warranted for 12 months from handover, excluding wear and tear, misuse and alterations by other parties.

8. Cancellation

Should the Client cancel after the works have commenced, the Client pays for all works completed and materials ordered up to the date of cancellation.

For any query on these terms, contact [Studio Name] at [Studio Phone Number]. Prepared by [Team Member Full Name].

quote_text_templates.title: Terms and Conditions for HDB Works
quote_text_templates.body:
TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR HDB WORKS

1. Renovation Permit

Works in an HDB flat are carried out under an HDB renovation permit applied for by [Studio Name], a Registered Renovation Contractor. The permit is valid for 3 months from its date of issue and works are scheduled within that period.

2. Permitted Hours

General renovation works are carried out between 9am and 6pm on weekdays and Saturdays. Noisy works such as hacking and drilling are limited to 9am to 5pm on weekdays and are not carried out on Sundays or public holidays.

3. Hacking and Structural Works

Structural walls, columns and beams will not be hacked. Wall demolition and floor hacking are carried out only where HDB has approved them and within the limits stated in the permit.

4. Wet Areas

Flats within their first three years from key collection keep HDB’s waterproofing on the bathroom floors; tiling in those bathrooms is carried out without disturbing the existing waterproofing membrane.

5. Disposal and Common Areas

Debris is bagged and removed daily. Common corridors and lift lobbies are protected during the works and left clean at the end of each day.

6. Payment and Warranty

Payment follows the schedule in this quotation. Workmanship is warranted for 12 months from handover. Prepared for [Client Full Name] by [Team Member Full Name], [Studio Name], [Studio Phone Number].

quote_text_templates.title: Terms and Conditions for BTO Works
quote_text_templates.body:
TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR BTO WORKS

1. Defects Check

Works begin only after the Client has completed the defects inspection with HDB’s Building Service Centre and the reported defects have been rectified, so that HDB’s defects liability period is not affected by the renovation.

2. Renovation Permit

[Studio Name] applies for the HDB renovation permit before any work starts. Optional Component Scheme fittings the flat came with are removed only where the Client has confirmed it in writing.

3. Timeline

A whole-flat renovation for a new BTO flat typically runs 8 to 12 weeks from commencement, depending on carpentry lead times and the confirmation of selections. The dates in this quotation are estimates.

4. Selections

Laminates, tiles, sanitary ware and fittings are to be confirmed before the works commence. Changes after an item has been ordered are variations charged at cost.

5. Payment and Warranty

Payment follows the schedule in this quotation. Workmanship is warranted for 12 months from handover. Prepared for [Client Full Name] by [Team Member Full Name], [Studio Name], [Studio Phone Number].

quote_text_templates.title: Working Hours and Site Access
quote_text_templates.body: Works are carried out from 9am to 6pm, Monday to Saturday. Please arrange for the keys or access card to be handed to [Team Member Full Name] before the commencement date, and register [Studio Name] with the building management where the estate requires it.

quote_text_templates.title: Material Lead Times
quote_text_templates.body: Laminate carpentry is fabricated 2 to 3 weeks after the drawings are confirmed; quartz worktops are cut 2 weeks after templating; imported sanitary ware and lighting take 4 to 6 weeks. Selections confirmed late move the dates in the schedule accordingly.

quote_text_templates.title: What This Quote Excludes
quote_text_templates.body: This quotation excludes the removal of existing furniture, electrical supply upgrades by SP Group, permit and management fees imposed by the authorities or the building, and items purchased by the Client directly. Contact [Studio Name] at [Studio Phone Number] to add any of these.

contract_templates.title: Interior Design Service Agreement
contract_templates.body:
Interior Design Service Agreement

This Agreement is made on Contract date between Studio name (UEN UEN ) of Studio address (the “Designer”) and Client name (the “Client”) for the renovation of Property address (the “Premises”).

1. Scope of works

The Designer shall carry out the design and renovation works described in quotation Quote number (the “Quotation”), which forms part of this Agreement. Works not listed in the Quotation are excluded unless agreed in writing as a variation under clause 5.

2. Contract sum

The contract sum is Quote total , inclusive of GST where the Designer is GST-registered. The sum covers labour, materials and workmanship as described in the Quotation.

3. Payment

Payment follows the schedule in the Quotation. Unless stated otherwise: 10% on signing; 30% on commencement of works; 30% on completion of carpentry; 30% on handover. Each invoice is due within 7 days. Works may pause while a payment is outstanding, and any such pause extends the programme by the same period.

4. Programme

Works commence within 14 days of the Designer receiving the signing payment and the permits the Premises require, and are planned to complete within the period stated in the Quotation. Dates are estimates: lead times for materials, third-party approvals and site conditions may move them, and the Designer will inform the Client of any change as soon as it is known.

5. Variations

Any change to the scope, materials or finishes requested after signing is a variation. The Designer will quote the variation in writing; works on it begin only once the Client confirms the quote. Variations may change the contract sum and the programme.

6. Materials and workmanship

Materials are supplied as specified in the Quotation or of equivalent quality. Natural materials such as stone, timber and veneer vary in colour and grain; such variation is not a defect. Workmanship follows the standard of good practice in the Singapore renovation trade.

7. Client’s responsibilities

The Client shall give the Designer access to the Premises during working hours, obtain any consent the Premises’ management requires, and make timely decisions on selections and approvals. Delays caused by late decisions or access extend the programme accordingly.

8. Defects liability

The Designer shall make good defects in workmanship reported in writing within 12 months of handover, at no cost to the Client. Wear and tear, misuse, and items installed by others are excluded. Manufacturers’ warranties on appliances and fittings pass to the Client on handover.

9. Termination

Either party may end this Agreement by 14 days’ written notice if the other is in material breach and does not remedy it within that period. On termination the Client pays for works completed and materials ordered to date; the Designer hands over the Premises in a safe condition.

10. Liability

The Designer’s liability under this Agreement is limited to the contract sum, and excludes indirect or consequential loss. Nothing here limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence.

11. Governing law and disputes

This Agreement is governed by the laws of Singapore. The parties shall first try to resolve any dispute in good faith, and failing that by mediation at the Singapore Mediation Centre before any court proceedings.

Signatures

Signed by the parties on the date first written above.

Studio signature

For Studio name 

Client signature

Client name , the Client

Agreement

contract_templates.title: Letter of Appointment
contract_templates.body:
Letter of Appointment

Contract date 

Dear Client name ,

Thank you for appointing Studio name (UEN UEN ) to design and renovate Property address . This letter confirms our appointment on the terms of quotation Quote number , for Quote total .

The deposit

On signing, a deposit of Deposit secures your project and starts the detailed design. The remaining payments follow the schedule in the quotation.

What happens next

Once the deposit is in, we confirm the works programme with you and apply for the permits your home needs. Any change to the scope after today is quoted to you as a variation before work on it begins.

Your acceptance

By signing below, you appoint Studio name for the works in quotation Quote number and agree to pay the deposit above.

Studio signature

For Studio name 

Client signature

Client name , the Client

contract_templates.title: Completion & Warranty Letter
contract_templates.body:
Completion & Warranty Letter

Contract date 

Dear Client name ,

We are pleased to confirm that the renovation of Property address (project Project number ) was completed and handed over to you on Completion date .

Defects liability period

Studio name will make good any defect in our workmanship that you report in writing within Defects period of completion — that is, by Defects period ends — at no cost to you. Fair wear and tear, misuse, and items installed by others are not covered.

Warranties

The manufacturers’ warranties on appliances, fittings and materials pass to you from the completion date. Please keep their cards and receipts with this letter.

Reporting a defect

Write to us at Studio email or call Studio phone , with photos where you can, and we will arrange a visit within 7 working days.

Thank you for trusting us with your home.

Studio signature

For Studio name 

Client signature

Received by Client name

project_updates.title: Hacking is done
project_updates.body:
All the old floor tiles and the kitchen counter are out, and the debris was cleared on Saturday.

The plumber marks the new water points on Tuesday — nothing needed from you this week.

project_updates.title: Flooring is laid in the living room
project_updates.body:
The oak vinyl is down in the living room and the skirting goes on tomorrow. The corridor follows on Friday.

Please keep off the floor for the next two days while the edges settle.

project_updates.title: Kitchen cabinets are in
project_updates.body:
The base and wall cabinets are fixed and the quartz top is templated — it arrives in about ten days.

The handles are the matte black ones you picked; the second photo is the moodboard we worked from.

project_updates.title: Wardrobe carcass is up in the master bedroom
project_updates.body: The wardrobe carcass is up along the window wall. Doors and the laminate go on next week.
project_updates.review_note: Add a close-up of the laminate — Benjamin asked about the finish.

project_updates.title: Feature wall panels have arrived
project_updates.body:
The fluted panels for the TV wall were delivered this morning, in the oak finish you chose.

They rest on site for two days before we fix them, so they settle to the room.

project_updates.title: Tiling is finished
project_updates.body: Floors and both bathrooms are tiled and grouted. The water test on both bathrooms passed this morning.

project_updates.title: Painting done — your home is nearly ready
project_updates.body: The walls and ceilings are painted and the whole flat has had its first clean. We start the handover check on the next working day — please keep an hour free to walk through it with Sarah.

project_updates.title: The water test passed in both bathrooms
project_updates.body:
All the points are in and tested. The water test on both bathrooms passed this afternoon — the report is attached.

Germaine marks the stage done once the last two kitchen points are covered.

project_milestones.title: Electrical & plumbing
project_milestones.resolved_note: Moved both kitchen sockets up to 1,100 mm, as on the drawing — the photos are in Updates.

project_schedule_shares.note: Here is the plan from start to handover. Electrical and plumbing finished today.
Here is the plan for your renovation — the dates move with the work.
All done — could you confirm the handover on your portal?

project_selections.title: Paint colours
project_selections.note: The living room and the three bedrooms take one colour; the ceilings stay white.

project_selections.title: Kitchen countertop
project_selections.note: The top goes on the base cabinets and the island; we template it once they are in.
project_selections.chosen_note: The Calacatta, please — with the waterfall edge we talked about.

project_selections.title: Bathroom tiles
project_selections.note: The wall and floor tiles for the common bathroom — the samples are at the studio if you want to see them.
project_selections.client_answer_note: Both feel too dark for a small bathroom — could we see something lighter, maybe a warm white or a pale terrazzo?

copilot_objection_log.objection_description: We’d like to move in before Chinese New Year.
copilot_objection_log.recommended_response: I completely understand wanting to move in quickly, especially if you are paying rent on top of your mortgage. The 6-10 week range accounts for HDB permit processing, material lead times, and proper curing periods for wet works. Rushing these stages often leads to defects that cost more to fix later. I will build in every efficiency I can and keep you updated weekly so there are no surprises.

copilot_objection_log.objection_description: Honestly the price feels a bit high compared with what we expected.
copilot_objection_log.recommended_response: I understand budget is a real concern, especially with the cost of living in Singapore. Let me walk you through exactly what is included in this quote — materials, labour, and project management — so you can see where every dollar goes. We can also look at phasing certain works or adjusting material grades to bring the total closer to your comfort zone without compromising the design intent.

copilot_objection_log.objection_description: We’re also comparing with another studio.
copilot_objection_log.recommended_response: That is absolutely the right approach — you should feel confident in whoever you choose. While you are comparing, I would encourage you to look beyond just the bottom-line price: check what is included in each quote, the warranty terms, and the payment structure. If you have any questions about our breakdown or want to do a like-for-like comparison, I am happy to help you make sense of it.

market_insights.title: Resale flats are reshaping the renovation brief
market_insights.excerpt: When more of a studio’s enquiries name a resale flat, the job changes: hacking, rewiring and re-tiling that a new flat rarely needs. What that changes in the first call, the site visit and the quote.
market_insights.content:
## Why resale changes the job

A new flat arrives as the developer left it: a studio plans around fresh walls, new wiring and tiles that can often be overlaid. A resale flat arrives with twenty or thirty years of someone else’s choices. Before anything new goes in, something old usually comes out.

For a studio, the shift shows in its own enquiries: a growing share of them name a resale flat. Here is how that can look for one sample studio.

```chart
{
  "type": "area",
  "title": "Share of enquiries naming a resale flat",
  "subtitle": "A sample studio's enquiries by year",
  "source": "Illustrative figures for the demo",
  "xKey": "year",
  "valueSuffix": "%",
  "data": [
    {"year": "2021", "share": 38},
    {"year": "2022", "share": 41},
    {"year": "2023", "share": 45},
    {"year": "2024", "share": 49},
    {"year": "2025", "share": 52},
    {"year": "2026", "share": 55}
  ],
  "series": [{"key": "share", "label": "Resale enquiries"}]
}
```

## What the extra work is

- **Hacking and disposal** — old built-ins, a kitchen, sometimes a wall the new layout doesn’t need.
- **Rewiring** — older flats often need new points, a new distribution board, or both.
- **Plumbing** — moving a sink or a washer point is common once the kitchen opens up.
- **Re-tiling** — an overlay is not always possible on old, uneven tiles.
- **Windows and grilles** — often replaced at the same time.

![An emptied living room, ready for the site visit — where the hacking and the rewiring are measured.](/market-insights/resale-empty.jpg)

## In the first call

1. Ask how old the flat is and whether it was renovated before.
2. Ask what the homeowner wants to keep — it is usually less than they first say.
3. Book the site visit before you quote. A resale quote written from a floor plan alone is the one that changes most later.

> **Designer tip:** keep a resale section in your quote — hacking, disposal, rewiring and re-tiling as their own lines — so a homeowner comparing quotes sees what a cheaper quote has left out.

## On the quote

Studios that do both kinds of job keep two starting points: one for a new flat, one for resale. In OpenMaison, save the resale lines once in [My Sections](/company/price-book/sections) and add them to any quote in one step.
market_insights.author: OpenMaison Editors

market_insights.title: Renovation budgets by flat type: how to read a benchmark
market_insights.excerpt: How a mid-range renovation budget steps up from a 3-room flat to an executive flat, and where a resale flat adds to it — a worked example of a benchmark, with illustrative figures.
market_insights.content:
## What a benchmark is for

A homeowner’s first question is nearly always “how much for my flat?”. A benchmark answers it with a range before anyone has measured anything — and tells the studio when a brief and a budget don’t match.

The ranges below are a **worked example**: a mid-range scope — paint, full carpentry for the kitchen, wardrobes and TV console, one or two bathrooms refreshed, a quartz worktop — with the figures made up to show how a benchmark reads.

```chart
{
  "type": "bar",
  "title": "Mid-range budget by flat type (S$)",
  "subtitle": "New flat and resale, the same scope",
  "source": "Illustrative figures for the demo",
  "xKey": "flat",
  "valuePrefix": "S$",
  "data": [
    {"flat": "3-room", "new": 30000, "resale": 39000},
    {"flat": "4-room", "new": 42000, "resale": 55000},
    {"flat": "5-room", "new": 52000, "resale": 67000},
    {"flat": "Executive", "new": 58000, "resale": 78000}
  ],
  "series": [
    {"key": "new", "label": "New flat"},
    {"key": "resale", "label": "Resale flat"}
  ]
}
```

## Why resale costs more for the same scope

| Work | New flat | Resale flat |
|---|---|---|
| Hacking and disposal | Little or none | Often a full day’s crew |
| Rewiring | Rarely | Often the whole flat |
| Plumbing | Minimal | Moving points is common |
| Tiles | An overlay is often possible | A full re-tile is common |
| Windows and grilles | Not needed | Often replaced |

## What moves a budget up

A premium scope adds on top of the mid-range one. The order matters more than the figures — stone and a full smart home move a budget most.

```chart
{
  "type": "bar",
  "title": "Adding to a mid-range scope (S$)",
  "subtitle": "One 4-room flat, each upgrade on its own",
  "source": "Illustrative figures for the demo",
  "xKey": "upgrade",
  "valuePrefix": "+S$",
  "data": [
    {"upgrade": "Stone worktops and vanity", "cost": 8000},
    {"upgrade": "Smart home, whole flat", "cost": 6000},
    {"upgrade": "Feature walls in three rooms", "cost": 5000},
    {"upgrade": "Designer fittings", "cost": 4000},
    {"upgrade": "Custom door hardware", "cost": 2500}
  ],
  "series": [{"key": "cost", "label": "Adds"}]
}
```

## Using a range with a client

1. **Lead with the range, then the scope.** “A 4-room resale at mid-range is usually in this band — where would you like to be?”
2. **Show what moves it.** The upgrades above are the conversation, not the small lines.
3. **Know your floor.** A quote far below your own range usually means scope has gone missing.

market_insights.title: Sample case study: a studio that calls every enquiry the same day
market_insights.excerpt: An invented three-designer studio shows what changes when every new enquiry gets a call the day it arrives — from the first call to the site visit and the signed quote.
market_insights.content:
## The studio

A three-designer studio in Tai Seng — invented for this sample — took most of its work from referrals and a listing site. Enquiries waited: a designer on site in the morning called back in the evening, or the next day.

## What they changed

1. **One owner for every enquiry** — the owner of the studio assigns each new lead within the hour.
2. **A call the same day** — before the end of the working day, from whoever owns it.
3. **Every call logged** — what was said and the next step, so a second designer can pick it up.
4. **The site visit booked on the call** — not “we’ll send some dates”.

```chart
{
  "type": "line",
  "title": "Days from enquiry to first call",
  "subtitle": "The sample studio, month by month",
  "source": "Illustrative figures for the demo",
  "xKey": "month",
  "valueSuffix": " days",
  "data": [
    {"month": "Jan", "days": 3.1},
    {"month": "Feb", "days": 2.4},
    {"month": "Mar", "days": 1.6},
    {"month": "Apr", "days": 1.0},
    {"month": "May", "days": 0.6},
    {"month": "Jun", "days": 0.4}
  ],
  "series": [{"key": "days", "label": "Days to first call"}]

```

## What it changed

More enquiries reached a site visit, and the visits were better prepared — the call had already covered the flat, the budget and the timing.


market_insights.title: Materials: what to check before you renew a quote
market_insights.excerpt: A quote written months ago can carry last season’s prices. A simple index shows how far worktops, laminate and tile can drift — and the four lines to re-check before you send a revision.
market_insights.content:
## Prices drift between a quote and a signature

A homeowner who takes three months to decide signs a quote whose prices were set three months ago. For most lines the difference is small; for a few it isn’t.

```chart
{
  "type": "line",
  "title": "Material prices, indexed to 2023",
  "subtitle": "2023 = 100",
  "source": "Illustrative figures for the demo",
  "xKey": "year",
  "data": [
    {"year": "2023", "worktops": 100, "laminate": 100, "tile": 100},
    {"year": "2024", "worktops": 104, "laminate": 103, "tile": 99},
    {"year": "2025", "worktops": 109, "laminate": 105, "tile": 101},
    {"year": "2026", "worktops": 113, "laminate": 106, "tile": 102}
  ],
  "series": [
    {"key": "worktops", "label": "Quartz worktops"},
    {"key": "laminate", "label": "Laminate"},
    {"key": "tile", "label": "Imported tile"}
  ]
}
```

## Re-check these four lines

1. **Worktops** — stone and quartz move most, and they are large lines.
2. **Carpentry finishes** — laminate and veneer ranges change with each new season.
3. **Tiles you import** — shipping, not the tile, is what moves.
4. **Appliances the studio supplies** — a model can be discontinued between quote and order.

![Stone and tile — the lines that move most between a quote and a signature.](/market-insights/materials-stone.jpg)

## Where the Price book helps

When a cost changes, change it once in [My Items](/company/price-book) — every new quote takes the new cost, and a revision can take it line by line.

market_insights.title: Where a renovation budget goes
market_insights.excerpt: A worked example of how a mid-range 4-room budget splits across the trades — carpentry, wet works, electrical and the rest — with illustrative figures, and how the split shifts for a resale flat.
market_insights.content:
## One budget, split by trade

Carpentry is usually the largest share of a mid-range renovation: the kitchen, the wardrobes, the TV console and the storage a homeowner asks for first.

```chart
{
  "type": "donut",
  "title": "A 4-room budget by trade",
  "subtitle": "A mid-range scope",
  "source": "Illustrative figures for the demo",
  "xKey": "trade",
  "valuePrefix": "S$",
  "data": [
    {"trade": "Carpentry", "amount": 22000},
    {"trade": "Wet works", "amount": 12500},
    {"trade": "Electrical", "amount": 7000},
    {"trade": "Plumbing", "amount": 5000},
    {"trade": "Painting", "amount": 4500},
    {"trade": "Air-conditioning", "amount": 4500}
  ],
  "series": [{"key": "amount", "label": "Budget"}]
}
```

## How resale shifts the split

The same scope in a resale flat spends more before carpentry starts — hacking, rewiring and re-tiling — so the other trades take a larger share of a larger budget.

```chart
{
  "type": "stacked-bar",
  "title": "The same scope, new and resale (S$)",
  "subtitle": "A 4-room flat",
  "source": "Illustrative figures for the demo",
  "xKey": "flat",
  "valuePrefix": "S$",
  "data": [
    {"flat": "New flat", "carpentry": 22000, "wet": 9000, "electrical": 4500, "other": 6500},
    {"flat": "Resale flat", "carpentry": 22000, "wet": 14500, "electrical": 9000, "other": 9500}
  ],
  "series": [
    {"key": "carpentry", "label": "Carpentry"},
    {"key": "wet", "label": "Wet works"},
    {"key": "electrical", "label": "Electrical"},
    {"key": "other", "label": "Everything else"}
  ]
}
```

## Reading it with a client

- **Show the split, not only the total.** A homeowner who sees that carpentry is the largest share knows where a saving can come from.
- **Name what a resale flat adds** before the quote, so the larger total is no surprise.

Nur: We collected the keys last month — a resale 5-room at Tampines St 24.
Nur: We want a modern kitchen and both bathrooms redone, and new flooring.
Dane: What budget are you working with?
Nur: Around 55k for everything.
Nur: My husband decides on the kitchen with me — he couldn’t come today.
Nur: We’re also talking to two other studios here.
Dane: Let’s meet again with your husband this week and walk through the kitchen.

hangout_meetings.scope: A new 3-bedder at Irwell Hill — kitchen, wardrobes and the living room feature wall
hangout_meetings.notes:
Kelvin: We get the keys in about three months — a new 3-bedder at Irwell Hill Residences.
Kelvin: We like warm luxury — marble, brass, dark wood.
Germaine: What budget do you have in mind?
Kelvin: About 90k, a bit more if the kitchen needs it.
Kelvin: We want you to do it. Can you send the quote next week?
Germaine: Yes — I’ll start the quote and send a mood board with it.
